title: Offline Replay Domain + Deterministic Scheduler
objective: Build CAN-X's first Replay domain, strictly OFFLINE. The source is a persisted DataSession; the output is an offline replay event/sink, never adapter.send(). This task must not add CanAdapter.send, python-can TX, hardware TX, a Safety Kernel authorization implementation, ARM state or a real bus replay; offline replay does not require TX authorization and real CAN replay (with a TX Safety Gate) is a later phase. Replay uses canonical recorded timing based on Frame.normalized_timestamp: relative_offset(frame_n) = normalized_timestamp(frame_n) - normalized_timestamp(first_frame), with speed defaulting to 1.0 (speed multiplier / pause / resume / step / loop / range belong to V0.4-09). A deterministic scheduler is built on an injectable clock abstraction (ReplayClock with monotonic() and sleep_until()/sleep()), with the production path using the real monotonic clock and tests using a fake clock, so deterministic tests never depend on asyncio.sleep(1.0) or wall-clock jitter. The same DataSession + replay configuration + clock behaviour must produce the same frame order, relative schedule, replay event order and terminal state. The canonical Frame is preserved in full (sequence, channel_id, arbitration_id, is_extended, is_fd, BRS, ESI, DLC, data, direction, timestamps, flags); offline replay never rebuilds an information-reduced Frame. Large sessions are read through the existing bounded QueryService pagination (DataSession -> bounded page -> scheduler -> sink -> next page), never loading a whole DataSession into memory. A minimal lifecycle is established: IDLE / RUNNING / COMPLETED / FAILED (an explicit STOPPED/CANCELLED may be added with stated semantics), with PAUSED / LOOPING / TRIGGER_WAIT left to later phases. The failure model covers an invalid project, an unknown session, a FAILED/incomplete session policy, a query failure, corrupted persisted data, a sink failure, a scheduler failure and cancellation, leaving no orphan replay task and never disguising a partial replay as COMPLETED.
scope: the new runtime/canx/replay/** domain package, its tests, and the V0.4-08 acceptance document.
non_goals: Any real CAN TX path, redirecting through a device adapter, or Safety Kernel authorization/ARM implementation
Replay speed/pause/resume/step/loop/range (V0.4-09), channel mapping/trigger/TX preparation (V0.4-10) or a Replay Desktop Workspace (V0.4-11)
Modifying runtime/canx/query/**, runtime/canx/recorder/**, runtime/canx/api/**, runtime/canx/devices/**, runtime/canx/safety/** or apps/desktop/**
Loading a whole DataSession into memory
acceptance_criteria: Replay is offline only: no CanAdapter.send, no python-can TX, no hardware TX, no ARM state, no Safety Kernel authorization implementation, no real bus replay
Relative timing is computed from Frame.normalized_timestamp; speed defaults to 1.0
An injectable ReplayClock (monotonic / sleep_until / sleep) is used with a real monotonic clock in production and a fake clock in tests; deterministic tests do not depend on wall-clock sleeps
Identical DataSession + configuration + clock behaviour produces identical frame order, relative schedule, replay event order and terminal state
The canonical Frame is preserved in full (sequence, channel_id, arbitration_id, is_extended, is_fd, BRS, ESI, DLC, data, direction, timestamps, flags)
Large sessions are read through bounded QueryService pagination; replay memory stays bounded
Lifecycle IDLE / RUNNING / COMPLETED / FAILED is established, no orphan replay task survives a failure or cancellation, and a partial replay is never reported as COMPLETED
A negative test proves the replay code has no adapter.send() call and no real CAN TX execution dependency
handoff_requirements: RED evidence first for each new behaviour
Exact commands and results for the targeted replay tests, the deterministic fake-clock suite, pytest -q, ruff and mypy
The negative test proving no adapter.send() call and no real CAN TX execution dependency
State explicitly that runtime/canx/query/**, runtime/canx/api/**, runtime/canx/safety/** and runtime/canx/devices/** are byte-identical to base_sha, and that no file outside allowed_paths was touched
